name: France
tagline: Public university costs €178 a year; the famous schools cost 100x that
summary: France is two systems. Public universities are almost free, and as an EU citizen you apply to them through Parcoursup, the national platform, over the winter. The grandes écoles and private schools, including Sciences Po, École polytechnique's bachelor and the business-school BBAs, run their own admissions and charge far more. Most English-taught bachelor's degrees are on that second side.
whyConsider: Public university tuition is among the lowest in Western Europe.
Serious English-taught bachelor's degrees at Sciences Po, École polytechnique and the business schools.
Parcoursup takes up to 10 wishes and you do not have to rank them.
watchOuts: The cheap public universities mostly teach in French.
Parcoursup wishes close in March and the grandes écoles' rounds close earlier still. Every offer is made before IB results, on predicted grades.
École polytechnique's first round closes on 20 October 2026, and its final round closes at 14:00, not midnight.
The 2027 Parcoursup calendar is not published yet. Re-check parcoursup.gouv.fr from December 2026.

sectorLandscape.summary: France splits between the universités, open to any qualified applicant, and the selective écoles: grandes écoles of engineering, business and political science, most reached through two years of classes préparatoires. Alongside them sit short vocational routes (the BTS in lycées and the BUT in university institutes of technology), public schools of art and architecture, and thousands of private schools.

routes.what: Three-year licence degrees at very low public tuition. Applied for through Parcoursup by EU students. Teaching is mostly in French.
routes.note: The ministry sends EU, EEA and Swiss nationals to Parcoursup for a first-year licence.

routes.what: Selective, often expensive schools. Several now run their own bachelor's degrees in English with direct entry after school: Sciences Po, École polytechnique's Bachelor of Science, the BBA and BSc programmes at ESCP, ESSEC, EDHEC and emlyon.
routes.note: Foreign-diploma applicants usually apply on the school's own platform, in rounds that close from October onwards.

routes.what: Two intense years in a lycée preparing for the competitive entrance exams of the grandes écoles. The traditional French route into an école, and almost unknown outside France.
routes.note: Taught in French. Not researched for IB applicants.

routes.what: The BTS is a two-year technician diploma taught in lycées; the BUT is a three-year practical degree at a university institute of technology (IUT). Both are applied for through Parcoursup.

routes.englishName: public school of art or architecture
routes.what: Public post-secondary schools of art (45) and of architecture (22), separate from the universities, each with its own selection.

jurisdictions.name: Public universities
jurisdictions.summary: Sorbonne, Paris-Saclay, PSL, Grenoble Alpes and Strasbourg. EU students apply through Parcoursup: up to 10 unranked wishes, closing in March.

jurisdictions.name: Grandes écoles and private institutions
jurisdictions.summary: Sciences Po, École polytechnique, ESCP, ESSEC, EDHEC, emlyon and the American University of Paris. Each runs its own admissions, usually in rounds, with its own fees.

variations.label: Rounds
variations.summary: Sciences Po closes 4 November 2026, 13 January and 1 March 2027. École polytechnique closes 20 October 2026, 6 January and 8 February 2027 (14:00).

notes: Grouped by sector rather than place: the kind of institution decides the route, not the region.
Corrected on this pass: the country profile said Parcoursup wishes are ranked. They are not; up to 10 are entered unranked (service-public.gouv.fr).
